v2_note: Keep factions as data (LOOP_V2 §11 step 1: 'three teams with factions as data'; LOOP_V2 §5: factions differ through uniforms) and keep colour as material roles. Drop the dead coat role or give it parts. In r128 a material colour is a uniform, so the faction recolour by itself adds no shader program (applyFaction core:643-653 and buildEntity core:657-669 change only .color per faction); what made 16 programs against 9 is not established (a spike can count programs per material parameter set). In v2, palette colours passed as uniforms or instance attributes keep one material for every faction, which also allows instancing. The team-to-faction mapping itself belongs to TEAMS (simulation data); only the palette is client-side.
reason: The role-based palette technique is client-side and worth keeping. The colour values wait for the look brief.

what: Walks a flat def.parts list and builds the mesh hierarchy. It creates 12 per-entity materials keyed by role, makes geometry from 9 primitive types (plus plain 'group' nodes), and tags each node (part, outlineW, matKind, role, noOutline, pid; every mesh casts shadows). It mounts the weapon and muzzle marker, maps the joints, sets a random animation phase and pelvisY, and applies the rest arm pose.
where: shamble-core.js:654-703 function buildEntity: mats 657-670, geomOf 671-682 (sphere, cyl, box, cone, torus, lathe, extrude, tube, plane), part loop 684-693, weapon mount 694-697 (hard-coded make 'AMKRifle' at 695), joints 698, userData 699-700, poseArms 701. Callers: shamble-game.js:130 (buildSoldier), shamble-editor.js:284 (Character Lab).
evidence: STATUS.md:84 and reports/2026-10-16-three-teams-core.md:74: about 120 draw calls per on-screen soldier. Same report :50: 1,480 draw calls with 12 soldiers on screen and 5,843 with 48. TECHNICAL.md:50: about 1 ms per soldier (re)build for outline normals (the look pipeline's share).
v2_note: Keep the data-driven recipe walker. At the 48+ target, cut the per-soldier draw calls, prune shadow casters and add LOD or instancing (STATUS:84); 5,843 draw calls at 48 is the known wall. Baseline (headless eval with tools/preview.js on the booted game, counting each soldier's group): a styled bot is 122-140 meshes, that is 66-77 primitive parts plus 56-64 ink hulls (the player 154); two of a bot's parts are the unlit health-bar planes (MeshBasicMaterial, game:797-798), and after stylizeScene every other part has its own toon material (distinct materials = parts; core:404). Every buildEntity part casts a shadow (core:686). The steps-1-6 report:94-95 counted 105 meshes and 49 outlines on 2026-10-16. The legacy code has no SkinnedMesh, InstancedMesh, BatchedMesh or LOD (grep over the three engine files: 0 hits). The parts animate independently, so the static merge (mergeStaticGroup, core:360-388, which bakes each part's transform into one geometry) cannot apply. Merging per material needs rigid skinning (one bone per part) or BatchedMesh with a transform per part; a spike measures draw calls and GPU time for each option at 48 soldiers on real hardware. Known quirk (code read, no render taken): setEnemyType (game:820) tints the head's material at game:3215, before stylizeScene at game:3363. The CHAR_MALE head uses the per-soldier shared 'skin' material (core:485), so every skin mesh of that bot takes the class accent colour. This matches the steps-1-6 report:59 note that arm and crest colours come from the unit, not the faction. The quirk persists because stylizeScene/toonify (core:404) makes one new toon material per mesh from the then-shared skin colour, so later setEnemyType calls (game:1842, 2939) recolour only the head. Also: userData.mats is stored but has 0 readers (grep), and docs drift: TECHNICAL.md:136/272 describe a buildCharacter shim that does not exist (only comments at core:9 and game:1258).
reason: Client-side procedural builder. Keep the recipe format; rebuild the mesh output for draw-call scale.

system: Procedural gun models (makeAMKRifle, _gunParts, makeBagpipeGun, makeShabzonSMG, makeLancerRifle, makeTorqueBow)
what: Builds one primitive-mesh model per gun, in a shared model space: the trigger grip sits near the origin and the barrel runs +Z. _gunParts supplies six materials (wood, dark, steel, brass, leather, glow) and add/box/cylinder helpers; the AMK rifle predates the helpers and builds its own two materials.
where: shamble-core.js:708-732 function makeAMKRifle (comment 704-707 is orphaned: it describes buildSoldier, which now lives in game), 734-740 GUN KIT header, 745-758 function _gunParts, 759-765 makeBagpipeGun, 766-772 makeShabzonSMG, 773-778 makeLancerRifle, 779-784 makeTorqueBow
evidence: AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:30 P6: each soldier caches up to 5 gun models (hidden); soak +63 objects, bounded, Low (AUDIT:15: heap 33.1 to 34.2 MB over 3 min, no leak). ANIMATION_PLAN.md §6: hand on grip/rail for all guns 0.0 cm [verified].
v2_note: Keep the model-space convention (grip at the origin, barrel +Z, outline weight tags). Avoid new materials per gun build: each call creates six (or two) fresh materials. These do not add draw calls (each mesh is a draw) and do not by themselves add shader programs (three.js shares programs between materials with the same parameters). They do prevent sharing and batching. Under the current look pipeline this is moot anyway, because stylizeOne/toonify (core:415, 278-286) gives every mesh its own new toon material. LOOP_V2 §5 adds a Recruit Luger pistol and a Javelin rocket, which have no model yet; UNITS.md:151 says the current guns are placeholders until progression is decided.
reason: Client-side procedural builders, cosmetic only. The convention ports; the shapes wait for the look brief.

The armMode enum is the contract the animation tick reads (game:288), and the _ARMP rest pose still decides the arms in the relaxed Lab pose and in melee mode with no visible prop. Port the enum and fold the rest pose into the animation port; the static tables need not survive as a separate system.

what: A law-of-cosines two-bone solver: given a shoulder (or hip), a target, a pole direction and two bone lengths, it sets the upper bone's quaternion and the elbow (or knee) bend, clamping reach so the limb never locks straight. It uses preallocated scratch vectors (zero allocation) and serves both arms and legs.
where: shamble-game.js:207-208 scratch vectors (_ikD, _ikDir, _ikAx, _ikUA, _ikLA, _ikQ, _ikQ2, _ikDown, _ikS, _ikT, _ikPole), 209 const ARM_L1/ARM_L2, 210-223 function solveArmIK. Calls: legs game:358, 472; arms game:415, 416, 427, 432, 435, 486, 488. The orphaned header comment is at shamble-core.js:813, directly above cabanaRepublicMap.
evidence: ANIMATION_PLAN.md §6 [verified, headless]: hand on grip/rail 0.0 cm, hands during reloads 0.0 cm, leg IK stretch 0.98 (target ≤ 0.98), katana left fist to hilt 2.7 cm, CPU per soldier per frame about 51 µs for the whole animation tick.
v2_note: Keep it: a small, allocation-free, well-measured solver. It is cosmetic only (ANIMATION_PLAN §1). The defaults ARM_L1 0.46 / ARM_L2 0.42 are labelled 'CHAR_MALE' but do not match the verified rig (upper arm 0.58, forearm 0.59, ANIMATION_PLAN §5). Every call passes its own lengths, so the defaults are unused and should not be carried over. Owned by the GA (game animation) area for everything around it.
reason: Client-side cosmetic animation math with verified accuracy. It ports nearly as is.

system: Melee and shield props (makeSword, makeAxe, makeShield)
what: Primitive-mesh melee props: a sword (used as the Beam Katana), an axe and a round wooden shield (iron rim, boss cone, four accent straps) whose boss material is kept in userData.boss for a block flash. All parts are marked noRay, hidden by default and hung on the player's hands. The block flash is set when a blocked hit lands on the player and decays each frame.

So the block flash writes to a material that no mesh renders. ANIMATION_PLAN.md §6 numbers (katana fist to hilt 2.7 cm, shield face vs aim dot 0.993) measure the holds in GA11, not these builders. ANIMATION_PLAN.md §7 says bots show no melee (it does not mention the shield). These props are built only for the player (game:3192-3194), and §8 item 2 lists bot shield and katana behaviour as future work.
v2_note: The axe is dead: no WEAPONS entry has id 'axe' (core:108-122), so game:1666 never picks it. The shield accent is a hard-coded teal 0x38e1b0, not a faction colour. Each prop makes its own materials. In LOOP_V2 §4 and §5 the Riot Shield and Banzai blade are class abilities unlocked at Tech 1. Whether the shield blocks shots is a simulation rule; these props only show it. The block flash is broken (confirmed by headless eval, no render). userData.boss (core:1471) holds the pre-toon MeshStandardMaterial. stylizeScene (core:404) and stylizeOne (core:415) replace every mesh material with a new toonify copy (emissive cloned, core:281), so game:2746 sets emissiveIntensity on a material no mesh renders while NPR is on (core:239 NPR=true). No WEAPONS entry has id 'sword' either, so the sword shows only for the katana. GA11 (area GA) owns the holds that use these props. Keep it cosmetic: no hit decision comes from these meshes (all noRay). Merged from CM14 on 2026-10-27, which listed the same builders from the CM line range.
reason: Client-side procedural props for kept abilities (shield, blade). Drop the unused axe.
